title: Formats: JSON, XML and YAML in network configuration

videos.script: NETCONF answers in XML. REST APIs and gNMI answer in JSON. And people write YAML, for inventories and playbooks. {{three}} Once a script has parsed any of them, it holds the same Python dictionary. The trouble is all at the edges. {{edges}} In XML, every name carries a namespace, and a search that forgets it finds nothing, and says nothing. {{xml}} In YAML, the country code of Norway becomes false, a version one point ten becomes one point one, and a port range becomes a number in base sixty. {{yaml}} A duplicate key in an inventory quietly replaces a router. And one interface comes out of XML as a dictionary, while two come out as a list. {{list}} In this lesson you meet each of these on purpose, with real output, and learn the checks that catch them before a device ever sees the data. {{checks}}
